article.title: Why Effective Sample Size Matters After Weighting

paragraphs.en:
Weighting is widely used in observational studies to make treatment and comparison groups more comparable. But after weights are applied, the number of rows in a dataset can become a misleading description of how much information the analysis really contains. This is why effective sample size, or ESS, matters.

Suppose an analysis has 100,000 customers. If every customer receives roughly the same weight, information is broadly distributed across the sample. But imagine that a small number of customers receive extremely large weights while most receive tiny weights. The dataset still contains 100,000 rows, yet the estimate may depend heavily on a much smaller set of observations.

A common formula for weighted ESS is the square of the sum of the weights divided by the sum of squared weights: ESS = (Σw)² / Σw². If all weights are equal, ESS is close to the nominal sample size. As weights become more unequal, the denominator grows and ESS falls.

This connects directly to inverse probability weighting. A treated person with a very small estimated probability of treatment can receive a large inverse weight. Such observations represent many other people in the weighted pseudo-population. They may help correct imbalance, but they also make the estimate sensitive to the outcomes of a few observations.

Consider two analyses that both start with 100,000 rows. Analysis A has an ESS of 92,000; Analysis B has an ESS of 18,000. Even if covariate balance looks similar, B generally contains much less weighted information for estimating the target contrast. Its standard errors may be larger and its result more sensitive to individual records.

ESS is therefore a useful diagnostic, not a magic acceptance rule. A low ESS does not automatically invalidate an analysis, and a high ESS does not prove causal identification. Analysts still need to examine covariate balance, overlap, model specification, the estimand, and the plausibility of no unmeasured confounding.

The measure should also be interpreted within relevant groups. For treatment-effect estimation, it can be useful to inspect the weighted ESS of treated and control groups separately. One side may retain substantial information while the other collapses because only a narrow region of propensity scores provides overlap.

Weight trimming or truncation can improve stability by limiting extreme weights. Stabilized weights are another option. But these choices can change the target population or reintroduce bias, so they should not be treated as cosmetic data cleaning. The analyst should state the rule, show sensitivity analyses, and explain the trade-off.

A good report might say: “The raw sample contains 100,000 observations, but after weighting the effective sample size is approximately 31,000, mainly because of extreme control-group weights.” That sentence is more informative than presenting the raw N alone.

ESS teaches a broader statistical lesson. Information depends not only on how many observations we collect but on how evenly those observations contribute to an estimate. When a few records carry most of the weight, a large dataset can behave like a much smaller one. Looking at ESS alongside weight distributions makes that hidden concentration visible and helps reviewers judge precision more realistically.
paragraphs.zh:
加權後的資料列數不等於真正的資訊量。若少數 observation 承擔非常大的 weight，估計結果就會高度依賴這些紀錄，即使 raw N 仍有十萬筆。常見 ESS 公式為 (Σw)²/Σw²；權重越不均，ESS 越低。

這與 inverse probability weighting 特別相關：propensity 很小的 observation 可能得到巨大 inverse weight，雖然有助於校正 imbalance，卻也提高 variance 與對個別紀錄的敏感度。因此應同時看 treated/control 各自 ESS、weight distribution、overlap、balance 與 estimand。

Trimming、truncation 或 stabilized weights 可以改善穩定性，但也可能改變 target population 或重新引入 bias，不能當成單純清理異常值。報告最好明確寫出 raw N 與 weighted ESS，並說明 ESS 降低主要來自哪一群的 extreme weights。
paragraphs.ja:
重み付け後は、データの行数がそのまま情報量を表すとは限りません。少数の観測に非常に大きな weight が付くと、raw N が10万件あっても推定結果は一部の観測に強く依存します。代表的な ESS は (Σw)²/Σw² で計算され、重みが不均一になるほど小さくなります。

IPW では傾向スコアが極端な観測に大きな逆確率重みが付きやすく、balance を改善する一方で variance を大きくする可能性があります。そのため treated/control 別の ESS、weight distribution、overlap、covariate balance、estimand を合わせて確認する必要があります。

Trimming や truncation、stabilized weights は安定性を改善できますが、対象母集団を変えたり bias を戻したりする可能性があります。raw N だけでなく weighted ESS も示し、どの群の extreme weights が情報量を減らしているか説明すると、推定精度をより正確に伝えられます。

vocabulary.usage: Nominal N may overstate information after weighting.
Poor overlap can produce extreme weights.
